name: The AI Stack — From Power to Products

openingQuestion.default: Where does an AI product actually get its capabilities?

energyPrompt.default: What happens when demand grows faster than power capacity?

chipsPrompt.default: What limits performance: compute, memory, or moving data?

infrastructurePrompt.default: How do we turn individual machines into a reliable service?

modelsPrompt.default: What makes a model useful for the task, beyond its benchmark score?

applicationsPrompt.default: What useful outcome does the product deliver for the person using it?

panelQuestion.default: Which layer is the bottleneck — and where would you build next?

children.text: Jensen Huang’s five-layer framework: start at power, end at products.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
Layer 1 · Power availability and cooling are physical constraints.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
Generation, grid access and dependable supply.
Cooling and facility efficiency shape capacity.
Layer 2 · Processing, memory and interconnects work as a system.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
From a chip to an AI factory.
Layer 3 · Connect, operate and serve the fleet.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
Layer 4 · Language, vision and other capabilities sit on the layers below.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
Use learned capabilities on new inputs.
Layer 5 · Products turn model capabilities into useful experiences.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
Help people think, create and work.
Connect intelligence to tasks and tools.
Bring the layers together: bottlenecks, economics and what builders should watch.
THE FULL SYSTEM, NOT JUST THE MODEL.
